name: Scotland
hook: Macbeth, Mary Queen of Scots, Robert Burns and Loch Lomond: the names Jeopardy keeps asking about.

facts.label: Mary, Queen of Scots
facts.statement: Mary, Queen of Scots was James VI's mother; she spent most of her teens in France and gave birth to the future king in 1566 while a prisoner.

facts.label: Macbeth
facts.statement: Shakespeare's Macbeth is the only play he set in Scotland; the real Macbeth killed King Duncan in 1040 to take the throne.

facts.label: Robert Burns
facts.statement: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet, the "Bard of Ayrshire," toasted in 1786 as "Caledonia's Bard."

facts.label: Glasgow
facts.statement: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city; its name comes from Celtic for "dear green spot," and it holds the Royal Conservatoire and University of Strathclyde.

facts.label: Loch Lomond
facts.statement: Loch Lomond is Scotland's largest lake by area; Loch Ness holds more water. Both are among its biggest lochs.

facts.label: Robert the Bruce
facts.statement: Robert the Bruce was crowned King of Scotland in 1306 and led the small force that won at Bannockburn in 1314, taking Stirling Castle.

facts.label: John Knox
facts.statement: John Knox fled to Geneva under Mary I, returned in 1559, and led the Reformation of the Church of Scotland.
